A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same single-vector false-refusal mitigation work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, vector-ablation experiments, parameter-sensitivity analyses and generated-response case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds Llama2-70B evaluations in Table 2. Its separately attributed baseline scores do not negate the presence of original results.

M1.justification: Difference-in-means extraction, refusal-score selection, KL filtering, partial orthogonalization and vector ablation remain unchanged. The new workflow and weight-editing appendix explain an implementation option already stated in v1; they do not establish a different algorithm.

E1.justification: The vector-construction sources and evaluation tasks remain the same, including OR-Bench-Hard, XSTest, OKTest, harmful-query tests and general-capability benchmarks. The added 70B model and additional comparisons use existing dataset/task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Appendix F and Table 4 add SafeDecoding, Self-CD and DRO to the XSTest comparison, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives beyond SCAN to include decoding and training-based approaches. Their scores are explicitly imported from Cao et al.; SCAN and the existing controls remain.

E3.justification: The main safety evaluator changes from LlamaGuard-3-8B to WildGuard, altering an important part of the evaluation protocol. Table 2 also adds Llama2-70B. V2 Appendix C.2 explicitly describes two-annotator checking for Table 3, whereas v1 described checking alongside Tables 2 and 3. These are reported protocol changes, not proof that every experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 4 removes the layer/token refusal-score maps for lambda = 0.4 and 0.8, retaining true-refusal maps and false-refusal maps at 0 and 0.6. The other parameter sweeps, vector-addition analyses and appendix case studies remain after matching their new locations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially revises reported results: Llama2-7B with ablation changes from 45.3 to 65.6 on ORB-H and from 57.6 to 42.4 on XSTest-S(H); Llama2-13B's ORB-H score changes from 36.7 to 26.7. V2 adds 70B results and three baseline rows in Table 4. Safety scores also change under the revised judge, preventing direct interpretation as same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: New Appendix D, equations 9–10, derives the equivalence between activation ablation and transforming an output weight matrix to W' = W - rr^T W. V1 asserted the equivalence without this derivation. The original method equations and assumptions are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim training-free, model-agnostic mitigation of false refusal while preserving safety and general capabilities, with adjustable refusal behavior and no additional inference cost. Abstract, introduction and conclusion revisions retain these contributions and their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix F extends the safety/helpfulness trade-off discussion to the additional baselines, identifying over-refusal as a particular drawback of DRO. Existing interpretations of vector separation, vector-addition costs and the limitations of data selection and first-token refusal scoring are substantially retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-release statement and repository link. Appendices B and D give more explicit intervention-location and weight-transformation details for attention and feedforward output projections. These improve implementation documentation without establishing a changed procedure.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to WildGuard and SafeDecoding and extends comparative positioning through Appendix F. The related-work sections and the central distinction from general refusal steering remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 polishes wording across the introduction, background, results and conclusion, and updates the publication header. It adds workflow, equivalence and baseline-comparison appendices while retaining the main section order and narrative; existing appendices are renumbered.

P2.justification: V2 adds workflow Figure 7 and baseline Table 4, an operation-description column in Table 1, and a 70B block with reordered safety columns in Table 2. Figure 4 is condensed and Figure 1 excerpts are shortened. These are localized display changes within the retained visual format.

improvement.justification: The workflow, weight-editing derivation and code-access information make the existing procedure easier to understand and reproduce. The 70B evaluation and broader baseline comparison improve empirical context. These benefits outweigh the limited loss of intermediate Figure 4 evidence, although unexplained Table 2 revisions and the changed safety judge limit conclusions about performance differences between versions.
